claim.why_it_matters: Every sub-entry indent on this page is dropped, including the first line 'Data-name 123', which the PDF indents because it continues the 'Subscripted' entry begun at the foot of page 1256. Flattened, it reads as a new top-level entry 'Data-name 123' rather than 'Subscripted > Data-name'. Same systematic defect as pages 1249-1254.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on all three legs; I tried to refute it and could not.

(1) The PDF quote is accurate. I rendered spec_p1257.png at 300 dpi and cropped the top-left column at 2x. The two-level index indentation is unambiguous in the printed glyphs: 'Data-name  123' starts at approximately x=260px, 'Subscripted identifier  124' at approximately x=110px, 'Subscripting  1030' at x=110, 'Condition-name  123' at x=260, 'Subscripts  122, 123' at x=110, 'Dynamic-capacity tables  157' at x=260, 'Substantive changes list  1172' at x=110. This is a clean alternation between a flush-left main-entry column and an indented sub-entry column, not ragged kerning. The same two-column indent pattern runs the full page in both columns (e.g. 'TO phrase' flush with 'ADD statement 583', 'INITIALIZE statement 637', 'INSPECT statement 643', 'MOVE statement 664' and five 'SET statement, ...' lines indented beneath it).

(2) The markdown quote is accurate and the loss is total, not partial. The page-1257 section of specs/ISO_COBOL.md (between the page-1257 and page-1258 anchors) contains 0 occurrences of ' ' and 0 lines beginning with a literal space, across 116 non-blank lines. Roughly 57 of those are indented sub-entries in the PDF. Nothing is reflowed onto an adjacent line and nothing is hyphenated or wrapped: the text is all present but the hierarchy carrier is gone entirely.

(3) This is a defect against the file's OWN convention, not a stylistic choice, which is the strongest refutation of a 'formatting only' reading. The transcription does encode index indentation elsewhere with a leading '    '. Indented-line counts by page: 1243=39, 1247=26, 1248=53, 1253=45, 1255=48, 1256=37, 1259=27 -- versus 1257=0 (and 1249-1252, 1254, 1258 also 0). Page 1257 is inside a run of pages where the marker was dropped.

(4) The 'why it matters' continuity claim checks out independently. The last non-blank content line of the page-1256 section is exactly 'Subscripted' with NO page reference -- a parent heading whose children begin on page 1257. Flattened, 'Subscripted' becomes a dangling entry pointing nowhere and 'Data-name 123' becomes a spurious top-level entry colliding with the genuine top-level 'Data-name' entry.

(5) Meaning is changed, so this is not page-break furniture. A flattened index inverts several lookups: 'Condition-name 123' reads as a top-level entry when the PDF makes it 'Subscripting > Condition-name'; 'Dynamic-capacity tables 157' reads as top-level when it is 'Subscripts > Dynamic-capacity tables'; 'ADD statement 583' reads as the top-level ADD entry when it is 'TO phrase > ADD statement' (page 583 is the TO-phrase discussion, not the ADD statement's own entry). Any consumer resolving 'where is X documented' from this index gets a wrong parent.

Only inaccuracy in the claim: the aside 'Same systematic defect as pages 1249-1254' over-generalizes -- page 1253 does retain its 45 indent markers. That does not affect the finding on page 1257.
verdict.corrected_description: Page 1257 (printed 1227), an index page, loses ALL sub-entry indentation in the markdown transcription: the page-1257 section of specs/ISO_COBOL.md contains zero ' ' indent markers and zero leading-space lines across 116 non-blank lines, while the PDF prints roughly 57 of them as indented sub-entries in a clear two-level layout spanning both columns. The transcription's own convention for index sub-entries is a leading '    ' (present on pages 1243, 1247, 1248, 1253, 1255, 1256 and 1259), so this is a dropped marker, not a formatting choice. Concrete meaning changes: the page's first line 'Data-name 123' is a child of 'Subscripted', the parent heading that is the final content line of page 1256 and carries no page number of its own -- flattening orphans that parent and creates a bogus top-level 'Data-name 123'. Likewise 'Condition-name 123' belongs under 'Subscripting', 'Dynamic-capacity tables 157' under 'Subscripts', and the nine lines from 'ADD statement 583' through 'SET statement, switch setting 729' belong under 'TO phrase'. The claim's PDF and markdown quotations are both verbatim-correct; its only error is the aside that pages 1249-1254 share the defect uniformly -- page 1253 retains its indentation.
